# `Q-1-16` — Object Property Count Violation

> An object has too few or too many properties for the schema's
> count constraint.

## What this means

Some schema entries restrict not which properties an object can
have, but *how many*. This error fires when an object has fewer
properties than the schema's minimum or more properties than the
schema's maximum.

This is distinct from `Q-1-10` (missing *required* property) and
`Q-1-18` (unknown property): a schema that limits property count
may accept any combination of property names so long as the count
stays in range.

## Why this happens

The pattern shows up most often where a schema models *exactly one
of N choices*: the object is allowed to set exactly one of several
mutually exclusive keys. Setting none triggers the minimum
violation; setting two triggers the maximum violation.

## How to fix

Re-read the schema for the property and identify which group of
keys it is enforcing the count over. If you set zero, add the one
key you mean to use. If you set more than one, decide which is
intended and remove the others — they likely represent alternative
ways of expressing the same thing.

## Related

- [`Q-1-10`](Q-1-10.qmd) — missing required property: this object has fewer
  properties than allowed, but at least one of them is required
  by name.
- [`Q-1-18`](Q-1-18.qmd) — unknown property: the schema accepts a known *set*
  of properties, regardless of count.
- [`Q-1-13`](Q-1-13.qmd) — array length: the same constraint applied to array
  items rather than object keys.
